bug_semantics: P2P download path accepts torrent pieces after CRC32-IEEE checks only, then CADownloadStore.MoveDownloadFileToCache commits the assembled blob under the requested SHA-256 digest with no whole-blob hash. A peer or on-path attacker can forge CRC32-matching piece bytes so attacker-chosen layers/manifests land in the content-addressable cache and are re-seeded. Upload-side CAStore.verify already recomputes SHA-256; the download path does not. GHSA-xpm6-xhxf-22h5 / CVE-2026-75625 remain published (not withdrawn/rejected).
flaw_origin: 5296d690e069c78d2df5bedec24611a9bb298ca9 (2017-11-21) replaced SHA-1 piece hashes with CRC32-IEEE, adding torlib/piece_hash.go (crc32.NewIEEE) and switching LocalTorrent.verifyPiece from sha1.New() to PieceHash()/Sum32. Parent 9c2ea795 still used SHA-1 piece hashes and had no piece_hash.go. Later cd2fcfc5 moved the file to core/piece_hash.go; HEAD still uses CRC32 and still moves downloads to cache without digest verify. Unmerged 908f36e6 (PR #641, branch thijmv/download-digest-verification) is not an ancestor of HEAD.

reasoning: CWE-354 cache poisoning is real on current main: CRC32 piece checks plus no SHA-256 of assembled download content. The advisory exploit (forged CRC32 pieces cached under a trusted digest) first became the piece-integrity design in 5296d690; the parent still hashed pieces with SHA-1. That BIC is a 2017 human Phabricator commit (Cody Gibb) with no AI markers, so authorship is NOT_AI. c20cbd6d first built torrent storage with SHA-1 pieces and is not this CRC32 mechanism. 98c286a8/cd2fcfc5 are moves/refactors. No merged fix: 908f36e6/PR #641 is unmerged, so fix_sha/direct_fix_sha stay null.
